utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are on this topic, with which we actually began with this witness, first of all, Witness, tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, could we please move into private session for a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I apologise for this, Your Honour. I neglected to tender this document during my cross-examination. Could I do that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P792, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when all of this was happening, you've already referred to it, but now I would kindly ask you to explain in more detail what it was that was happening in your environs, the place where you lived, at that time.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: As I said during the examination-in-chief, the Red Berets and the Patriotic League and especially the paramilitary forces of Juka Prazina whom I could see myself from the house of Zarko Pajic. There were Juka and several other people with rifles as early as September and they caused disquiet with the Serbian population. Those are the things that I could see, although I didn't mention them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Much was said here about you allegedly fleeing the scene. Can you explain to me what ensued in the next following days? It says here that you fled. Please explain what was going on.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: I did not flee, as I said. The next day I was in my post office working, as well as for the next seven days. I went to work and went back home. I did not move anywhere else. On the eighth day there was a military vehicle with two military policemen which arrived at around 8.00. They came to arrest me and a cousin of mine with a court order. They were told to bring us down to the prison in the Viktor Bubanj barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When did they learn of your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: In the barracks, in the Viktor Bubanj facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the proceedings that followed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, first I spent 29 days in custody there, after which I was released and I continued working in the post office as of the 20th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what the police did -- sorry. Based on what the military court did, what happened with this action?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: It fell through. All of the arms were taken by the military from the police. Nothing else was done. The entire proceedings which followed were dealt with by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were in that prison how long?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Twenty-nine days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the sanction imposed on you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: There was also a fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And after October until April, did you have any weapons in your hands?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: No, not until April. I didn't even come close to a weapon, let alone hold one in my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As the Prosecutor insisted on this, can you explain your military training. How did it come about that you were awarded this rank? First of all, do you have any military training?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And where did you acquire this training?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: While I was serving in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is what you should explain. This was when you were a young conscript.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes. I was 19 years old when I went to serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This was in 1983, as you said. After that, you had nothing to do with the military.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you serve in the army in 1983?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: For 15 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours, with reference to the hills, we dealt with Debelo Brdo and an area we could talk about. But please tell me, does the hill of Mojmilo overlook anything in that area?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Not in that area. The hill of Mojmilo controls on all three sides both parts under BH army control and parts under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. Mojmilo controls three municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about Zuc, Hum, and Grdonj? What do they overlook?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: On the northern side there is no other hill overlooking those three hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Mount Igman is and what it overlooks?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Mount Igman is to the southwest of Sarajevo and it overlooks all the other hills. It's the highest mountain near Sarajevo, and from positions on that mountain, one can control Hadzici, Ilidza. It had the most dominant elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned another hill in connection with mortars. You said it was in the rear. How high was it?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Oh, Prljavo Brdo, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: I don't know the exact elevation. It was about the same height as Lukavica. Maybe some 30 metres higher than Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when Dragomir Milosevic was the commander, were there any mortars there?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we take a look at this document. It's Prosecution Exhibit P667.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The document is unsigned. You allowed for the possibility that it's a telegramme. You said you knew nothing about this document personally. But it says here, "I order." And then look at subparagraph 2 of paragraph 1 and read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: "These weapons are to be used only to rebuff Muslim attacks. They should be used against targets in the area only on orders from the corps commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So the decisions that reached you, what form were they in? When I say that, I mean were they in writing, like this, or did you receive them in some other way?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: The battalion commander conveyed those decisions to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And were they always in the same spirit, that weapons were to be used only to rebuff a Muslim attack?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, can you just explain to me a little more what your role precisely was on that truck.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, in the end I understood that I was supposed to go with the driver and unload something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the witness will say, but he might mention a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll go into private session, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That was my point, too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave. We will adjourn for a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the next witness is?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next witness is T52. He arrived yesterday and I only had time to shake hands with him and say hello, but I did not have any time to talk to him. I was planning to do that today. The health complication has arisen in the meantime, but it was not possible to call the next witness here today. We were counting on having two witnesses which would have filled all of today and part of tomorrow. But the witness who was supposed to testify today had a health problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So this arises from the illness of yesterday's witness. You have no backup witness, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next witnesses are arriving today. We have not been late with witnesses so far. But the next witnesses will be testifying after the weekend. We were planning to complete both witnesses tomorrow, so each second would have been filled. The health problems of this witness have disrupted all our plans. It was an act of God, it was not up to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In those circumstances, it seems unavoidable. We adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
